side-tab.plain: A card with one thick coloured stripe on a single edge. It is the most recognisable sign of a generated interface.
side-tab.technical: FAIL when an element at least 120 x 48 px has exactly one border of 3 px or more with a saturated colour and nothing on the opposite side. Mark state with a badge, tint or icon instead.

border-accent-on-rounded.plain: A thick coloured edge on one side of a rounded box. The straight stripe fights the curve of the corner.
border-accent-on-rounded.technical: WARN when a one-sided accent border sits on an element with a corner radius of 8 px or more. Drop the border or the radius.

nested-cards.plain: A card inside a card. Each extra frame adds noise and fake depth without adding meaning.
nested-cards.technical: WARN when a card-like container (radius, padding of 12 px or more, and a border, fill or side border) has another card ancestor within three levels. Buttons and other controls do not count as cards.

justified-text.plain: Body text stretched to both edges leaves uneven word gaps that read as rivers of white.
justified-text.technical: WARN when text-align: justify is set on a block with 80 or more characters of its own text. Use text-align: left, or hyphens: auto with lang set.

skipped-heading.plain: Heading levels that jump, such as h2 straight to h4, break the outline that screen readers and search engines follow.
skipped-heading.technical: WARN when a heading is more than one level deeper than the one before it in document order. Choose the level for structure and set the size with CSS.

token-contrast.plain: A pair of colours in your tokens that is too faint to read, in at least one theme or contrast mode.
token-contrast.technical: FAIL, unwaivable. Every declared pair is resolved in every mode permutation and measured: 4.5:1 for body text, 3:1 for large text and UI parts. The report names the permutation and the pair.

reduced-motion-ignored.plain: Something keeps moving after the system asked for less motion.
reduced-motion-ignored.technical: FAIL. The capture reruns each cell with prefers-reduced-motion: reduce; anything still moving (transform, position or size, or transition: all) for more than 10 ms fails, by CSS or Web Animations. Opacity and colour changes are exempt.

theme-unresponsive.plain: The page looks the same whether the system is set to light or dark, so it ignores a preference people chose.
theme-unresponsive.technical: WARN. The capture compares a fingerprint of computed colours (text, background, border, fill, color-scheme on up to 300 elements) in the light and dark cells; identical fingerprints mean prefers-color-scheme is not honoured. A page that stores a theme but starts from the system setting passes.

contrast.plain: Some text is too faint against its background to read comfortably.
contrast.technical: FAIL when text is under 2.6:1 (unreadable); WARN above that but below the WCAG need of 4.5:1 body or 3:1 large text. Measured on the rendered page against the real background behind each text run.

grey-body.plain: Body copy set in a soft grey that looks refined and tires the eye.
grey-body.technical: WARN when the main running text is under 7:1 against its ground. Keep the muted ink for secondary notes only.

gradient.plain: Any gradient fill. Generated pages lean on them for atmosphere, and they quickly look alike.
gradient.technical: FAIL when a gradient fill is found. The one allowed gradient is a neutral scrim over a photo to keep text legible.

emoji.plain: Emoji in the interface, usually as icons or bullets. They look different on every platform and cannot be themed.
emoji.technical: FAIL when emoji appear in visible page text. Use words, a real icon set or imagery.

shadow.plain: Cards lifted off the page by a soft shadow when they are just sitting on it.
shadow.technical: FAIL on marketing pages for at-rest shadows; off in apps. Separate surfaces with a tone step or space and keep shadows for things that really float: menus, dialogs, sticky bars.

heavy-shadow.plain: Panels in an app drawn so heavy they look like floating sheets.
heavy-shadow.technical: FAIL in apps when a panel shadow is heavy enough to read as floating. Panels sit on the ground: use a fill one step from the ground or a hairline.

glass.plain: Blurred translucent surfaces layered over a background. One quiet bar is fine; many cards is a tell.
glass.technical: WARN on marketing pages when more than one element uses a backdrop blur.

hairline.plain: Thin grey lines drawn round and between everything to organise the page.
hairline.technical: FAIL when two or more hairline rules or dividers are found on a marketing page, WARN for one. Use fill steps, space and type to separate.

eyebrow.plain: A tiny uppercase label above a heading, repeated on every section until it becomes furniture.
eyebrow.technical: FAIL when eyebrow or kicker labels sit above headings. Say it in the heading, or drop the label.

size-count.plain: Too many different font sizes, so no size means anything.
size-count.technical: WARN above 9 distinct font sizes. About five carry a page: display, heading, lead, body, small.

body-size.plain: Body text that is too small to read comfortably.
body-size.technical: FAIL under 15 px; WARN under 16 px on desktop. Body copy sits at 16 to 20 px.

measure.plain: Lines of text so long the eye loses its place going back to the start of the next line.
measure.technical: WARN when the longest paragraph runs more than 88 characters per line on desktop. Aim for 45 to 75 with max-width in ch.

font-count.plain: Too many typefaces on one page. Each added family dilutes the voice and slows loading.
font-count.technical: FAIL above three families, WARN at three. Two at most: one display and one text, and often one is enough.

font-fallback.plain: A font was named but did not load, so the browser quietly used a stand-in. What you reviewed is not the design.
font-fallback.technical: WARN when a declared typeface is not loaded and a fallback renders. Fix the URL or family name.

focal-point.plain: The first screen has nothing that leads: no big headline and no dominant picture.
focal-point.technical: FAIL on marketing pages when the largest type is small and no single picture fills a third of the viewport. Make one thing lead.

small-text.plain: Blocks of text so small that many people cannot read them.
small-text.technical: FAIL when more than three text blocks are under 13 px, WARN for one to three. Nothing meant to be read goes below 13 px.

tiny-text.plain: Labels and data set in near-microscopic type inside an app.
tiny-text.technical: FAIL when more than two text blocks are under 11 px; WARN when under-13 px text exceeds 45% of the text.

side-scroll.plain: A row that scrolls sideways with its content cut at the edge. Most people read the cut as clipped, not scrollable.
side-scroll.technical: WARN when a row scrolls horizontally with content beyond its edge. Wrap it onto more lines or end it with a clear scroll cue.

overflow.plain: The whole page scrolls sideways at this screen width, which almost always means something is too wide.
overflow.technical: FAIL when horizontal overflow exists at the tested viewport. The report names the widest offending elements.

tabular.plain: Numbers in tables that do not line up, so columns of figures are hard to compare.
tabular.technical: WARN when fewer than half of six or more figures use tabular numerals. Set font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums on table cells and figures.

rainbow-chart.plain: A chart that uses every colour in the paintbox, so no series stands out and colour stops meaning anything.
rainbow-chart.technical: FAIL above six hues in charts, WARN above four. One accent for the series that matters, neutrals for the rest.

colour-sprawl.plain: Too much of the app screen is strongly coloured, so colour no longer signals anything.
colour-sprawl.technical: WARN when more than 12% of the first screen is strongly coloured. Keep the screen neutral and spend colour on data and status.

radius-mix.plain: Panels with many different corner radii look unplanned.
radius-mix.technical: WARN above three distinct radii on panels. One radius for panels, one for controls, full round only for pills and avatars.

placeholder-data.plain: Obvious stand-in content on screen: lorem ipsum, "John Doe", numbers that do not add up.
placeholder-data.technical: FAIL when placeholder names or text are found. Use believable data for this product, with units and dates in order.

icon-cards.plain: A row of identical cards each topped with a small icon and two lines of text.
icon-cards.technical: FAIL when a row of structurally identical cards each topped by a small icon is found. Replace it with one composed section built around a single idea.

all-centred.plain: Nearly everything is centred, so the eye has no edge to follow down the page.
all-centred.technical: WARN when over 72% of the text is centre-aligned on a page with four or more headings. Centre one moment; anchor the rest to a shared left edge.

default-link.plain: Links still showing the browser default blue and purple, so they look unstyled.
default-link.technical: WARN when the default link colours (#0000ee, #551a8b) are rendered. Style every link and mark it with more than colour.
